title: MultiValue database family tree
note: Transcribed from the MultiValue history chart (1965 to today). Branches: TRW, PICK, REALITY, PI. Before diverging, Pick R77 ≈ REALITY 3.x ≈ PI 1.0. derived_from / leads_to follow the chart's arrows (IP ownership or source code).

entries.name: IBM (hardware)
entries.description: IBM hardware on which TRW built the original GIRLS/GIM system in 1965.

entries.name: GIRLS → GIM
entries.description: The first system in the MultiValue family tree, built by TRW in 1965 on IBM hardware. GIRLS was later renamed GIM; GIM-I, GIM-II, RIS and ITDS all derive from it.

entries.name: GIM-II
entries.description: TRW's GIM-II, derived from GIM and run for the CIA on DEC PDP-11 hardware.

entries.name: CIA
entries.description: User of GIM-II on PDP-11 hardware.

entries.name: PDP-11 (hardware)
entries.description: DEC PDP-11 minicomputer that ran GIM-II for the CIA.

entries.name: GIM-I
entries.description: TRW's GIM-I, derived from GIM and run for NASA on Univac hardware.

entries.name: NASA
entries.description: User of GIM-I on Univac hardware.

entries.name: Univac (hardware)
entries.description: Univac hardware that ran GIM-I for NASA.

entries.name: RIS
entries.description: Product of General Analytics, derived from TRW's GIM; feeds into Pick & Associates' ACCESS/DM512.

entries.name: ITDS
entries.description: US Army system derived from TRW's GIM.

entries.name: Xerox Sigma 7 (hardware)
entries.description: Xerox Sigma 7 hardware on which Pick & Associates built ACCESS / DM512.

entries.name: ACCESS, DM512
entries.description: Early Pick system from Pick & Associates on Xerox Sigma 7, influenced by TRW's GIM; the start of the Pick branch.

entries.name: Multi-6
entries.description: Pick derivative that took source code from Pick & Associates.

entries.name: Pick Systems R77 / R80 / R81
entries.description: Pick Systems' releases R77, R80 and R81. Before the branches diverged, Pick R77 was roughly equivalent to REALITY 3.x and PI 1.0.

entries.name: Evolution
entries.description: Pick derivative from the R77 era of Pick Systems.

entries.name: Omnus → ICC
entries.description: Pick derivative from Pick Systems, Omnus later became ICC.

entries.name: Pick Systems R83 / R84 / OA / Adv Pick / AP PRO
entries.description: Pick Systems' 1980s–90s releases: R83, R84, Open Architecture (OA), Advanced Pick and AP PRO.

entries.name: Pick AT
entries.description: Pick version for PC AT-class machines, from Pick Systems' R83 line.
derived_from: Pick Systems R83 / R84 / OA / Adv Pick / AP PRO

entries.name: Pick Blue
entries.description: Pick version from the Pick Systems R84 line (see also the Seattle Labs Pick Blue port for IBM RT/RS6000).
derived_from: Pick Systems R83 / R84 / OA / Adv Pick / AP PRO

entries.name: D3
entries.company: Pick Systems → PickAX → Raining Data → TigerLogic → Rocket
entries.description: Pick Systems' D3 (1990s). Its IP passed to PickAX, then Raining Data → TigerLogic; today D3 is a Rocket product.
derived_from: Pick Systems R83 / R84 / OA / Adv Pick / AP PRO

entries.name: PickAX
entries.description: Company that took over Pick Systems' IP; passed to Raining Data → TigerLogic.

entries.name: Datamedia
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Datamedia hardware.

entries.name: Xmark
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Xmark hardware.

entries.name: Altos → Acer
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Altos hardware (later Acer).

entries.name: C.Itoh (CIE) → GA
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for C.Itoh (CIE) hardware (later GA).

entries.name: CDI IBM Series/1
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for CDI IBM Series/1 hardware.

entries.name: WICAT
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for WICAT hardware.

entries.name: Fujitsu → Alpha Micro
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Fujitsu hardware (later Alpha Micro).

entries.name: Fujitsu España
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Fujitsu España hardware.

entries.name: Tau/Nippon
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Tau/Nippon hardware.

entries.name: Pick Vulture
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Pick Vulture hardware.

entries.name: MDC Eagle board
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for MDC Eagle board hardware.

entries.name: DEC VAX & MicroVAX
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for DEC VAX & MicroVAX hardware.

entries.name: SMI IBM 370, 4300, 9370
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for SMI IBM 370, 4300, 9370 hardware.

entries.name: Sanyo/ICON AT&T & BSD UNIX
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Sanyo/ICON AT&T & BSD UNIX hardware.

entries.name: Upboard
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Upboard hardware.

entries.name: Pertec Sabre → Scan-Optics
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Pertec Sabre hardware (later Scan-Optics).

entries.name: ICL Clan → STC
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for ICL Clan hardware (later STC).

entries.name: Archford Excalibur
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Archford Excalibur hardware.

entries.name: IBC
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for IBC hardware.

entries.name: Electronique Serge Dassault
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Electronique Serge Dassault hardware.

entries.name: Seattle OS → Seattle Labs Pick Blue IBM RT/RS6000
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Seattle OS hardware (later Seattle Labs Pick Blue IBM RT/RS6000).

entries.name: Pinnacle
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Pinnacle hardware.

entries.name: Toltec → Edge → Edgcore → Arix
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Toltec hardware (later Edge, Edgcore, Arix).

entries.name: Rexon Summit → Alpha Micro Pick 64+ → Sequoia → GA
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Rexon Summit hardware (later Alpha Micro Pick 64+, Sequoia, GA).

entries.name: Aston Crystal Excel
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Aston Crystal Excel hardware.

entries.name: Pyramid → Siemens
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Pyramid hardware (later Siemens).

entries.name: DS-Rabbit
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for DS-Rabbit hardware.

entries.name: Data General
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Data General hardware.

entries.name: Encore
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Encore hardware.

entries.name: Climax Sunshine
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Climax Sunshine hardware.

entries.name: Stratus
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for Stratus hardware.

entries.name: XEROX Brazil
entries.description: Port of Pick: a licensed implementation of Pick for XEROX Brazil hardware.

entries.name: Zebra
entries.description: General Automation's Pick implementation (Other SMA Pick).

entries.name: R91
entries.description: General Automation Pick release, successor to Zebra.

entries.name: Power 95
entries.description: General Automation Pick release, successor to Zebra.

entries.name: SequoiaPICK
entries.description: Pick implementation from COST → Sequoia; led to mvEnterprise.

entries.name: mvEnterprise
entries.description: Successor to SequoiaPICK; IP later passed to General Automation.

entries.name: mv.PRO
entries.description: Product derived from mvEnterprise; IP later passed to General Automation.

entries.name: Mentor
entries.description: ADDS' Pick implementation, later owned by NCR ADDS → AT&T.

entries.name: M-PC/OS
entries.description: PC version of Mentor from NCR ADDS → AT&T.

entries.name: MentorPRO
entries.description: Successor to Mentor from NCR ADDS → AT&T.

entries.name: M-O/E
entries.description: Successor to M-PC/OS.

entries.name: mv.BASE
entries.description: Derived from Mentor/mvEnterprise; IP passed to General Automation, then Raining Data → TigerLogic. Today mvBase is a Rocket product.

entries.name: UniVision
entries.description: Pick-style database coded from scratch by EDP → Kerridge.

entries.name: General Automation (2000s)
entries.description: General Automation in the 1990s–2000s, owning Zebra, mvEnterprise, mv.PRO and mv.BASE IP; passed to Raining Data → TigerLogic.

entries.name: Honeywell (hardware)
entries.description: Honeywell hardware for which The Ultimate Corp. built its Pick implementation.

entries.name: Ultimate
entries.description: The Ultimate Corp.'s Pick implementation on Honeywell hardware; led to Ultplus.

entries.name: Ultplus
entries.description: Successor to Ultimate; IP passed to OSS → Nextech.

entries.name: OSS → Nextech
entries.description: Company that took over Ultplus IP.

entries.name: Intertechnique (hardware)
entries.description: Intertechnique hardware on which Réalité ran.

entries.name: Réalité
entries.description: Intertechnique's French Pick implementation; led to IN2, then Siemens Nixdorf.

entries.name: IN2
entries.description: Successor to Intertechnique's Réalité; IP passed to Siemens Nixdorf.

entries.name: Nixdorf
entries.description: Siemens Nixdorf Pick implementation, from IN2.

entries.name: Microdata (hardware)
entries.description: Microdata hardware on which Reality was built.

entries.name: Reality (Microdata)
entries.description: Microdata's Reality, the start of the REALITY branch. Reality 3.x was roughly equivalent to Pick R77 and PI 1.0.

entries.name: Reality 3.x … 5.x … 7.x … REALITY/X
entries.company: Microdata → CMC → McDonnell Douglas → MDISI → MDIS
entries.description: Reality releases as ownership moved Microdata → CMC → McDonnell Douglas Corporation → McDonnell Douglas Computer Systems Company → MDISI → MDIS; later Northgate Information Solutions.

entries.name: (PC)microReality
entries.description: PC version of Reality.

entries.name: M9000/Sequel/Sequoia
entries.description: Reality derivative (M9000, Sequel, Sequoia); led to Pegasus and Spirit.

entries.name: Pegasus
entries.description: Product derived from M9000/Sequel/Sequoia.

entries.name: Spirit
entries.description: Product derived from M9000/Sequel/Sequoia.

entries.name: JAC
entries.description: Company that started jBASE; led to jBASE Software.

entries.name: jBASE
entries.description: MultiValue database coded from scratch by jBASE Software; passed to Temenos (jBASE → TAFC) and Temenos → jBASE Int'l / Mpower1. Today jBASE is a Zumasys product.

entries.name: jBASE → TAFC
entries.description: Temenos' version of jBASE, renamed TAFC; led to TAFJ.

entries.name: TAFJ
entries.description: Temenos product coded from scratch, successor to TAFC.

entries.name: Caché
entries.description: InterSystems' database, coded from scratch, shown alongside the MultiValue family.

entries.name: Reality (ADP)
entries.description: ADP's Reality; IP later passed to ADP → CDK (CoRA).

entries.name: CoRA
entries.description: ADP → CDK product derived from ADP's Reality and jBASE.

entries.name: Devcom
entries.description: Company in the REALITY/PI area, linked to the PI branch.

entries.name: VAR Consortium
entries.description: Group of value-added resellers linking the REALITY and PI branches.

entries.name: PRIME (hardware)
entries.description: Prime Computer hardware on which PRIME INFORMATION was built.

entries.name: Information
entries.description: PRIME INFORMATION, coded from scratch by Prime: the start of the PI branch. PI 1.0 was roughly equivalent to Pick R77 and Reality 3.x.

entries.name: PI/Open
entries.description: Prime's open-systems successor to PRIME INFORMATION.

entries.name: ComputerVision
entries.description: Company that took over Prime's PI IP.

entries.name: Revelation (COSMOS)
entries.description: COSMOS' Revelation, coded from scratch; led to Revelation's RevG and Arev, and today's OpenInsight.

entries.name: RevG
entries.description: Revelation product (Revelation G), successor to COSMOS' Revelation.

entries.name: Arev
entries.description: Advanced Revelation, successor to RevG; led to OpenInsight.

entries.name: PI/PC
entries.description: PC version of PRIME INFORMATION, linked to RevG.

entries.name: OpenQM
entries.description: MultiValue database coded from scratch by Ladybridge; led to ScarletDME. Today OpenQM is a Zumasys product.

entries.name: ScarletDME
entries.description: Open-source MultiValue database derived from OpenQM.

entries.name: URMA → mvON
entries.description: Coded from scratch; URMA was later named mvON and led to ONgroup's MVON.

entries.name: Netbasic → MVON
entries.description: ProSolutions' Netbasic, coded from scratch and later named MVON.

entries.name: MVON
entries.description: ONgroup's MultiValue product, from mvON and ProSolutions' Netbasic → MVON.

entries.name: UPIX
entries.description: Alfa's PI-compatible product, coded from scratch.

entries.name: uniVerse
entries.description: VMark's uniVerse, a PI-style database; IP passed to Ardent, Informix, then IBM. Today UniVerse is a Rocket product.

entries.name: FIRESTORM
entries.description: Data General product derived from VMark's uniVerse.

entries.name: pcVerse
entries.description: Profile's PC product derived from uniVerse.

entries.name: Ardent
entries.description: Formed from VMark (and Unidata); owned uniVerse and UniData IP before Informix.

entries.name: Informix
entries.description: Took over Ardent's uniVerse and UniData IP; passed to IBM.

entries.name: UniData
entries.description: Unidata's UniData, coded from scratch; IP passed through Pacific Unidata/Ardent/Informix to IBM. Today UniData is a Rocket product.

entries.name: Pacific Unidata
entries.description: Company that owned UniData IP before IBM.

entries.name: Raining Data → TigerLogic
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of D3 and mvBase, from Pick Systems/PickAX and General Automation.

entries.name: Temenos → jBASE Int'l / Mpower1
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of jBASE.

entries.name: Ladybridge (2000s)
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of OpenQM.

entries.name: Northgate Information Solutions
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of REALITY, from the Microdata/McDonnell Douglas line.

entries.name: Revelation
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of OpenInsight, from Revelation/RevG/Arev.

entries.name: IBM
entries.description: Early-2000s vendor of UniData and UniVerse, from Informix and Pacific Unidata.

entries.name: D3 (Rocket)
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Rocket, descended from Pick Systems' D3.

entries.name: mvBase
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Rocket, descended from mv.BASE.

entries.name: jBASE (Zumasys)
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Zumasys, descended from jBASE.

entries.name: OpenQM (Zumasys)
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Zumasys, descended from Ladybridge's OpenQM.

entries.name: REALITY
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Northgate Public Services (an NEC company), descended from Microdata's Reality.

entries.name: OpenInsight
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Revelation Software, descended from Revelation and Arev.

entries.name: UniData (Rocket)
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Rocket, descended from Unidata's UniData via IBM.

entries.name: UniVerse
entries.description: Current MultiValue database from Rocket, descended from VMark's uniVerse via IBM.
